failures.symptom: assertEqual(FloatValidator.getInstance().validate1(strSmallestPositive, pattern), smallestPositive) fails: got None instead of sys.float_info.min (~2.2250738585072014e-308)
failures.likely_cause: FloatValidator._processParsedValue in src/main/org/apache/commons/validator/routines/FloatValidator.py clamps parsed values to true IEEE-754 32-bit single-precision bounds (_FLOAT_MIN_VALUE ~1.4e-45, _FLOAT_MAX_VALUE ~3.4e38) computed via struct pack/unpack, rejecting (returning None for) any value outside that narrow range. The oracle's Python fixtures use Python's native double-precision float (sys.float_info.min/max, ~2.2e-308/~1.8e308) as the expected representable range, so the 32-bit clamp under/overflows and returns None instead of the value.
failures.repair_hint: In FloatValidator.py, remove (or widen) the 32-bit single-precision min/max range check and the narrowing struct.pack/unpack('<f',...) round-trip in _processParsedValue; parsed floats should be returned as ordinary Python doubles without clamping to Float.MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE bounds, matching how Python has no distinct float32 type.
